thread.title: Scientists Investigate Dark Energy's Nature and Implications for the Universe
thread.title_full: Scientists Investigate Dark Energy's Nature and Implications for the Universe

author: ADITHI RAMAKRISHNAN
title: Scientists Investigate Dark Energy's Nature and Implications for the Universe
text:
• Dark energy makes up nearly 70% of the universe.
• Dark energy is causing stars and galaxies to move away from each other at an increasing rate.
• Scientists are exploring whether dark energy is a constant force or if it is weakening.
• Recent findings presented at the American Physical Society meeting suggest dark energy may be waning.
• The research comes from an international collaboration creating a three-dimensional map of galaxy distribution over 11 billion years.
• The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument has analyzed nearly 15 million galaxies and quasars.
• Previous analyses included 6 million galaxies and quasars.
• Other measurements, such as exploding stars and distortions in galaxy shape, support the idea of weakening dark energy.
• The collaboration aims to map around 50 million galaxies and quasars by 2026.
• Other global efforts, including the European Space Agency’s Euclid mission, are also investigating dark energy.
• If dark energy is constant, the universe may expand indefinitely.
• If dark energy weakens, the universe could eventually stop expanding and collapse in a Big Crunch.
• The implications of dark energy's behavior could significantly alter current cosmological theories.
